request: Analyze GSE195707 for PMID 35325353 (Senolytic treatment rescues blunted muscle hypertrophy in old mice.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq, plantaris muscle, old (23-24 mo) male C57BL/6J mice (S2.8.p1, S2.2.p1)
final.primary_estimand: Effect of senolytic D+Q (vs vehicle) on the plantaris transcriptome of old mice after 14 days of synergist-ablation mechanical overload (MOV, the paper's resistance-exercise model) (S2.8.p1, S3.5.p1)
final.sample_inclusion: Paper RNA-seq: vehicle- and D+Q-treated old mice, 14 d MOV, n=5/group (S2.8.p1; FIG6 N=5/group). GEO also deposits sham-operated vehicle and D+Q mice (n=5 each), not analysed by RNA-seq in the paper.
planned_contrasts: D+Q vs vehicle at 14 d MOV (S3.5.p1; paper: ~2,000 DEGs, Fig. 6a)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none; one plantaris per mouse, independent animals
final.normalization: Partek E/M gene counts, minimum expression cutoff of 10 counts (S2.8.p1)
final.paper_results: ~2,000 DEGs D+Q vs vehicle; down: Ddit4, Cryab, TCA/ETC genes; up: Igf1, Fmod, Dcn, Mmp14, Adamts1, Plau, 7 ADAMTS members (S3.5.p1)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.8.p1 defines the RNA-seq: plantaris from vehicle and D+Q old mice 14 d after MOV, n=5/group, Partek E/M counts, filter 10 counts, DESeq2 FDR<0.05. S3.5.p1 reports ~2000 DEGs. The exercise stimulus (MOV) is common to both arms in the paper's contrast; the paper's estimand is how senolytic treatment modifies the exercise-induced transcriptome, not MOV vs sham. MOV vs sham contrasts are identifiable from the deposited sham samples and are run as exploratory.

checks: GEO: Mus musculus plantaris, age 2 years, treatment Senolytic/Vehicle, surgery Overload/Sham, protocol text matches S2.4.p1/S2.3.p1
20 samples = 4 groups x 5; paper's 10 MOV samples are a subset

ownership.reasoning: Data-availability statement DA.p1 names GSE195707; GEO treatment protocol (D+Q 5/50 mg/kg on days 7 and 10 of 14-day MOV) and data_processing (Partek Flow, STAR 2.7.8a, Partek E/M, GRCm39, release 103) match S2.4.p1 and S2.8.p1.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns (OS14d5, OVS4, OV14D5 ...) equal metadata 'description' exactly for 20/20 (inspect alignment_keys). Codes are consistent with titles (OS14d=old senolytic 14d overload, OSS=old senolytic sham, OV14D=old vehicle 14d overload, OVS=old vehicle sham). Factors from the GEO characteristics columns.

matrix.reasoning: GEO says 'raw counts' but 30% of values are non-integer (e.g. 3735.96, 729.999), consistent with Partek E/M expectation-maximization estimated counts (data_processing). Library sizes 17.9-26.2 M, median 50: count scale, not FPKM/TPM. Paper input to DESeq2 is the same Partek E/M counts (S2.8.p1). Round to integers for DESeq2. 20 gene symbols repeat (distinct Ensembl genes sharing a symbol); summed per symbol.

final.analysis_type: factorial (2x2); paper contrast is the simple effect of treatment within MOV

design.reasoning: Paper's planned contrast is D+Q vs vehicle within 14 d MOV (S2.8.p1, S3.5.p1). The deposited 2x2 (treatment x surgery, n=5/cell) also identifies the exercise-model effect MOV vs sham within vehicle and within D+Q, and the treatment x surgery interaction (does D+Q change the MOV response); these are exploratory, fitted in one cell-means DESeq2 model on all 20 samples. Old male mice only, so no sex stratification.

candidates.value: pooled MOV vs sham across treatments
candidates.reason_rejected: pooling treatment levels hides the treatment factor; simple effects within each treatment plus interaction used instead

covariance.reasoning: One plantaris per independent mouse; no batch, lane or pairing recorded in GEO and none stated in the paper.

final.formula: ~ trt (MOV subset); exploratory joint model ~ cell (2x2 cell means)

paper_route.method: DESeq2 (Partek Flow) two-group on MOV samples, FDR<0.05

deviations: pydeseq2 instead of Partek Flow DESeq2 v3.5
Partek 'minimum expression cutoff of 10 counts' interpreted as mean raw count >= 10 across the analysed samples (exact Partek rule not stated); sensitivity with count >= 10 in at least one sample
E/M estimated counts rounded to integers

method.reasoning: Paper used DESeq2 on Partek E/M counts (S2.8.p1); the deposited matrix is those counts, so the paper method is reproducible after rounding.

threshold.reasoning: S2.8.p1: DESeq2 (FDR<0.05); no fold-change cutoff stated.

caveats: Paper's RNA-seq estimand is D+Q vs vehicle under MOV (senolytic modification of the exercise-model response), not exercise vs sham; MOV vs sham and interaction are exploratory, not reported by the paper.
Partek low-count filter rule ambiguous; count comparison depends on it.
Synergist ablation is a model of resistance-exercise overload, not voluntary exercise.

study.reasoning: Paper reports approximately 2,000 DEGs (S3.5.p1); named genes from S3.5.p1/FIG6 (Ddit4, Cryab down; others up).
